BetterRailwaySystem changes minecart motion by targeting the worst parts of vanilla rail gameplay first.
Powered rails no longer behave like an immediate jump to a fixed top speed. Instead, the mod applies progressive acceleration and deceleration based on config values.

The current implementation prioritizes: better high-speed curve handling better slope handling reduced derailment risk preserved momentum, similar to the effect of the newer experimental minecart improvements

When another minecart is ahead on the same path, the system tries to maintain a configurable safe distance. If a collision becomes unavoidable, braking behavior can become more aggressive. This does not guarantee that all collisions can be avoided.
Minecarts without passengers can be despawned after a configurable unattended timeout. This is useful for long-running servers where inactive carts would otherwise accumulate.
Some BetterRailwaySystem systems depend on both the client and the server having the mod installed.

If a client connects to a server that does not expose BetterRailwaySystem networking: map requests are blocked server-backed asset sync is blocked related UI paths show a clear disabled message instead of trying to continue
On a modded server, synchronized assets allow: server-stored transponder images server-stored transponder sounds redistribution to online clients automatic sync for joining players
On dedicated servers, asset upload is intended to be restricted to trusted users such as operators. This avoids turning the media pipeline into an unrestricted file upload surface.
The operational block set is where BetterRailwaySystem moves beyond pure physics tuning.
Use railway transponders for: arrival and departure broadcasts passenger-facing announcements speed-limit sections BossBar updates
Use stop rails for: approach-based stopping dwell timing redstone-based release reliable restart logic
Use spawners for: assigning city and line identity choosing direction maintaining a target number of active minecarts circular-line dispatch workflows
Use collectors for: end-of-line removal route recording finalization preventing entity buildup on completed lines
The map system turns repeated train operation into reusable line data.

BetterRailwaySystem uses custom payloads for gameplay screens and synchronized media.
The main payload groups include: opening block editors saving block settings requesting line maps clearing saved map data asset upload and asset synchronization
The server stores route data such as: city name line ID direction station list line color station coordinates

Synchronized media currently uses: client-side staging for upload preparation server-side asset storage redistribution to clients as chunked payloads local resource-pack regeneration on the receiving client
The mod is split into a small number of focused packages.

org.dcstudio.minecart Minecart behavior, state access, route recording logic, and supporting enums. org.dcstudio.station Railway block classes and block entities such as balises, stop rails, spawners, and collectors. org.dcstudio.network Client/server payloads and synchronization entry points. org.dcstudio.renderer Client UI screens, overlays, and route map rendering. org.dcstudio.config Config model, persistence, and commands.
org.dcstudio.client Client initializer, config UI entry points, and client networking. org.dcstudio.client.asset Local resource-pack generation and synchronized asset handling.

BetterRailwaySystem supports both singleplayer and dedicated multiplayer, but multiplayer requires a consistent setup.

Install Fabric Loader for Minecraft 1.21.1. Put the BetterRailwaySystem jar into the client mods folder. Put Fabric API into the same folder. Put Cloth Config into the same folder. Launch the game and verify the mod loads without errors.

Prepare a Fabric server for Minecraft 1.21.1. Put the BetterRailwaySystem jar into the server mods folder. Add Fabric API. Add Cloth Config. Accept the Minecraft EULA and complete the normal Fabric server setup.

If you want the full feature set, both sides should run the mod: Client only gives you the local mod files, but server-backed features will not work on an unmodded server. Server only is not enough, because clients also need the mod to render UI, overlays, and receive synchronized assets correctly.
ModMenu is optional for clients and is not required on dedicated servers.
BetterRailwaySystem currently expects: Minecraft 1.21.1 Fabric Loader Fabric API Cloth Config Java 21+ ModMenu (client only)

If the client joins a server that does not run BetterRailwaySystem: line-map requests are disabled server asset upload and sync are disabled other server-backed operations are gated off instead of trying to run incorrectly
After installing the mod, verify these items before building a larger railway system.
Open the redstone tab and confirm these blocks are visible: railway transponder stop rail train spawner train collector
Open the config screen and confirm you can see editable values for: max speed acceleration deceleration safe following distance unattended despawn time
Create a short powered-rail test line and confirm: the minecart accelerates smoothly the minecart slows smoothly on unpowered powered rails no obvious startup errors appear in logs

If you are testing on a server, also verify: the server starts with the mod installed both client and server have the required dependencies the client can open BetterRailwaySystem screens on that server asset sync requests do not show the “server missing” message

BetterRailwaySystem is a Fabric mod for Minecraft that improves the vanilla minecart system without replacing vanilla rails or turning the game into a separate transport simulator. Core goals: keep vanilla rails change and add selected vanilla minecart behaviors add some features commonly found in real railway systems

This documentation site is organized into five sections: Introduction: a general introduction to the mod. Installation: client, server, and dependency setup. Tutorials: basic operations. Advanced: system behavior and multiplayer workflows. Developer: code structure and implementation direction.
If you are new to the mod, read the pages in this order: Design Goals Client and Server Installation First Line First Balise
The goal is to make the vanilla railway system easier to use, closer to real-world railways, while still keeping vanilla interaction patterns.
Players should continue using vanilla rails, powered rails, detector rails, activator rails, and redstone logic. The mod should not force a separate placement system or parallel rail ecosystem.
BetterRailwaySystem does not add a completely new minecart entity family, such as fully realistic train models or rail visuals. Instead, it directly extends the behavior of the vanilla minecart.
The mod adds value in areas where vanilla minecarts feel limited: acceleration train dispatch and recovery onboard announcements stop control route recording line visualization (WIP)

Railway systems become much more interesting once multiple players use them together. That is why dedicated server support, synchronized station media, and client feature gating are part of the design.

build a full standalone metro simulator replace vanilla rail placement with custom infrastructure blocks require custom train entities for core features abandon singleplayer in favor of server-only workflows

Because the project stays close to vanilla rails, some systems must work around vanilla constraints. That tradeoff is intentional. The mod prefers compatibility and maintainability over building a separate, incompatible railway game inside Minecraft.
This page summarizes the main feature groups currently implemented in BetterRailwaySystem.

smooth acceleration on powered rails smooth deceleration on unpowered powered rails configurable top speed, acceleration, and deceleration configurable minecart top speed based on tick substeps reduced derailment on curves automatic following-distance braking behind another minecart on the same path

one minecart can carry multiple players all passengers share the same vanilla minecart entity each player keeps readable local first-person and third-person rendering other onboard player models are hidden to avoid stacking and clipping
railway_balise stop_rail: stop rail train_spawner: train spawner train_collector: train collector
station visits can be recorded into a world railway map city and line grouping is supported current line maps can be opened while riding a world railway map can be opened while not riding

dedicated servers are supported balise images and sounds can be uploaded from a client to a modded server synchronized media is redistributed to online players when the server does not run the mod, client-side features that depend on server networking are disabled
railway_balise is the core block for station-side event triggers.
You will replace the block under the rail with one transponder and make a minecart trigger an onboard event.

Place a railway_balise. Open its configuration screen. Choose a mode such as announcement or arrival. Optionally set current station, next station, title, subtitle, image ID, and sound ID. Ride a minecart through the trigger area.

Depending on the mode and fields you set, the cart passengers should receive: optional title/subtitle text optional current-station and next-station information optional BossBar updates optional image and sound playback
media identifiers must exist on the current client, or come from a synchronized server asset library only the passengers of the triggered minecart receive the announcement
This tutorial gets you to a working first line as quickly as possible.
a short rail loop or shuttle one minecart at least one powered section a test ride for speed behavior

Place a short vanilla rail line. Add powered rails and power them with redstone. Put a minecart on the track. Ride the minecart and observe the acceleration behavior. Add one unpowered powered rail segment and observe the smoother braking behavior.
acceleration should feel progressive instead of immediate the cart should hold momentum better than vanilla in many cases braking should not look like a hard instant stop
After this, continue with First Balise to add your first station event.
This tutorial extends a basic line and transponder setup into a complete route.
Set up a train_spawner and make a route that can be recorded into the world railway map.

Replace the block under a valid rail position with train_spawner. Open the spawner UI. Set a city name. Set a line ID. Pick a line color. Set the direction. Set the target train count. Add one or more transponders on the route. Place a train_collector at the end, or make the route circular if that matches your design.
When the minecart completes the line: visited stations should be recorded line color should be preserved the route can later appear in the world railway map (WIP)
Keep station naming consistent when building transfer stations. Shared names inside the same city are treated as interchanges in the map. (WIP)
This tutorial explains the current synchronized asset workflow.
the server must run BetterRailwaySystem the client must also run BetterRailwaySystem on dedicated servers, the uploading player should have operator-level permission

Open the asset library from the transponder editor. Click Open Folder. Drag .png or .ogg files into the upload staging folder. Return to the game and click Refresh. The client uploads staged files to the server. The server stores them and re-broadcasts the asset library to online clients. Connected clients reload the synchronized media into their local resource pack.
the same identifiers can be used across players on that server newly connected players can receive the server library on join
